slide.title: Git is asked once per command
slide.takeaway: Each command or request asks Git through one session; answers are kept only while they cannot change: by ref digest, or by immutable commit ID.

item.label: One Git session per command or request
item.description: gitexec.Begin opens one session per CLI command and BeginIsolated one per reviewer request; nested calls share it, output is memoized by arguments, and the outermost end() stops its processes.

references.note: Begin, BeginIsolated and the session they attach.
Begin, BeginIsolated and the session they attach.
Begin, BeginIsolated and the session they attach.
A session memoizes per session, a nested Begin shares it, and end() stops its processes.

criterion_links.rationale: A comparison resolves its base, head and merge-base inside one session, so Git is asked each question once per command.

item.label: Long-lived cat-file batch process
item.description: ResolveCommit, ReadObject and object lookups share one cat-file --batch-command per repository, pooled up to GOMAXPROCS; after repeated failures callers fall back to a one-shot git process.

references.note: Revision and object reads through the batch process.
Revision and object reads through the batch process.

criterion_links.rationale: The revisions a comparison names are resolved to commits through the session's cat-file process.

item.label: diffCommits shares one diff-tree process
item.description: Diffs of two full commit IDs go through one diff-tree --stdin process per format and pathspec, whose output is what git diff prints; other revisions, or a failed process, run git diff itself.

references.note: diffCommits and its one-shot fallback.
diffCommits and its one-shot fallback.

criterion_links.rationale: The canonical diff it returns is the set of changed lines that coverage classifies as covered, uncovered, overlapping or stale.

item.label: Ref and config answers kept by state digest
item.description: TopLevel, RepoOutput, ConfigOutput and branch or HEAD commits are kept across commands and served only while a digest of HEAD, refs, packed-refs and every config file is unchanged.

references.note: The ref-state cache and the digest that guards it.
The ref-state cache and the digest that guards it.

criterion_links.rationale: The checkout a Saga lives in is found with TopLevel, answered from this cache while the repository's refs and config are unchanged.

item.label: Stable answers of immutable commit IDs
item.description: Ancestry, merge-base and diff answers of full commit IDs are kept in a 64 MiB LRU, served only after cat-file confirms the objects still exist, never with grafts, shallow or replace refs, and never for failures.

references.note: The Stable cache and its safety checks.
The Stable cache and its safety checks.
The Stable cache and its safety checks.
Stable keeps successes across sessions, never failures, and forgets pruned commits.

criterion_links.rationale: The merge-base of two commit IDs never changes, so compare mode reads it from Git once and then from this cache.

item.label: The server keeps commit diffs per request
item.description: A nested .gitattributes edit can change a patch and no cache key covers it, so serve marks the process long-running and each request's isolated session keeps its diffs only until the response is written.

references.note: withGitSession and the isolated diff store.
withGitSession and the isolated diff store.
withGitSession and the isolated diff store.
An isolated session ignores a diff cached before a nested attributes edit.

criterion_links.rationale: The reviewer re-reads commit diffs for each request, so its coverage never classifies lines from a patch read before an attributes edit.
